name: stirred_ink
description: a poured liquid stirred into S-curls and hooks: smooth bands of one glossy ink, combed along the level lines of a turned copy of the fractal, with bright crests glowing along the folds and the curls tightening towards the set
reuses: the smooth count through the matched map by rank
light (molten_flow's slope relief on the smooth count), masked off the lace by the distance
adds: the stir: passes that carry each sample's point along the level lines of a viewed copy of the fractal before anything is iterated (engine/src/stir.rs)
notes: From meditation-25 and vibe-25 (item 058), with wallhaven-5gqrp3 and polished-25 as further readings and wallhaven-47xzoe as ring_pools. The first style with a stir: the layers are molten_flow's relief and two sheet rims; the look is where they are drawn. molten_flow lays three views' level lines over the frame as translucent sheets; here two views' level lines carry the frame itself, so there are no sheets and no lace on top, only the one ink combed into curls.

Round one (Matt, 4/5 for the paint-like readings he picked; the readings he did not pick 1/5; only the blue map liked): kept f_wide at both seats, f_strong at the first and two locations drawn with round one's stack. The default is now f_wide, kept at both seats: the first copy at zoom 0.35, period 2, capped at 0.2 of the frame. The next paragraph describes round one's stack (the two location keeps' own).

The stir is two passes at angle 90 (along the copy's level lines). The first copy is turned 100 degrees at zoom 0.8, strength 3 over 4 steps, swinging every 3 escape steps, capped at 0.08 of the frame: the large S-curls. The second is turned 220 degrees at zoom 1.5, strength 2 over 3 steps, period 2, capped at 0.04: the finer hooks inside them. One pass alone (round one's first drafts) already reads as poured liquid; the second keeps curls at more than one scale in open field.
The copy must differ from the frame. A pass on the frame's own count (view straight) at angle 35 scratched dark hatching across the lace and showed no curl; it left the drafts.

Calming the lace: the relief is masked by the distance (log), so the light fades on the set and the lace does not turn to pebbles under it; the map is read by rank at gamma 1.6, so the far field stays in the dark blues. The crests are two sheets on the stirred count, cut by the stretch (not rank) at 5 bands: a thin rim (edge 0.03) near the map's white and a wide one (edge 0.3) at 0.8 for its glow.

Round one's readings, as formulations; all but f_strong and f_wide kept nothing, and the ember entry left the library with its map: f_strong (strength 6 over 8 steps and 3 over 4: longer windings), f_wide (the first copy at zoom 0.35, period 2, largest 0.2: a few frame-wide swirls over the finer pass), f_gloss (the relief unmasked at slope 1.5 with a rim), f_crest (9 bands of crests on a darker ground), f_blobby (polished-25: one pass at strength 1.6 under a four-band ringed light, in the glossy_lobes map), f_pour (wallhaven-5gqrp3: matte poured paint, the relief nearly flat, tone 0.2/0.05, 14 ranked bands each edged in the map's ultramarine with a dark seam between), f_nostir (the stack without its stir), and the entry stirred_ink_ember (vibe-25, tone 0.196/0.045: the map's navy to steel by rank at 0.7 of a cycle, and 12 ranked crests laid `normal` in its ember top under a screened ember glow; a screened orange rim alone turns mauve over blue, and crests cut by the stretch grow into salmon slabs in open field).

Open water (f_open, a further reading in round one): at scouted seats with wide far field the stack already reads closest to meditation-25, as broad glossy waves with glowing fold lines; f_open gives them a steeper relief (slope 1.2, unmasked gamma 2.3), four thin crests and a gentler second pass (strength 1.2). Three of its four seats run brighter than the reference (p90 0.85 against 0.71, near-white 0.05 to 0.06). Two darker re-tunes (map cut to 0.82 or 0.9 of a cycle at gamma 2.3 and 3.4) fixed p90 and broke p10 instead (0.30 and 0.38 against 0.22): with so little structure the tone pass lifts the whole frame, so the fix is in the crests and the light, not the albedo. The ember entry on the same seats and relief (e_open_ember: eight ranked crests, edge 0.04, glow edge 0.12) is the closest reading of vibe-25 in the round and holds its tone at all four (median 0.205 to 0.214 against 0.196, p90 0.43 to 0.46 against 0.49).

Cost: 7 steps, each three escape loops with the Jacobian the light and the mask ask for, so 22 loops a sample. A 1280x800 ss2 draft took 4 to 15 s at six threads at shallow cubic Julia seats (maxiter 7000 to 10000) and 30 to 80 s at four threads at the scouted seats, where the samples close outside a copy's set run most of the way to the seat's cap. In `style-wasm` on one thread a 640x400 ss2 frame took 141 s (ring_pools, one pass and no Jacobian: 28 s): too slow for a live explorer view as it stands, and round two's first question if Matt keeps it. One pass, fewer steps, or a Jacobian carried through the loop's own derivative instead of two more runs would each cut it. Quiet (068), 1280x800 ss2 on one thread: 117 to 143 s at the shown keeps' seats, 314 s at the deepest kept seat (maxiter 20293), the one over the explorer bar; without the light (and so the Jacobian) about a third of that, without the stir under a tenth (ratios at 320x200). Dropping the fine pass (230 s) or the wide pass at 3 steps (289 s) are look changes, Matt's picker `quiet_speed_cuts_068`; a page maxiter of 10000 there bought nothing (343 s).

The stir's first build read the orbit's smooth count and the library's `sin`, and the module then drew about 600 visibly different samples of 256,000 (13,380 differing at all): the native engine and wasm link different maths libraries, and seven steps of push near the set magnify their last bit. The stir now makes its own logarithm and sine from the exact operations, and native and module agree byte for byte.
